messages:
Mira: kicking off a coverage/parse-safety sweep for the new raven-liteq int4 bring-up. goal: measure funcall JSON compliance across temps, streaming vs non-streaming, and batch sizes.
Arjun: can you paste the exact matrix?
Mira: matrix: CPUs: canary-dedicated-gpu x2, quant modes: int4/int8, temps: 0.0/0.3/0.7, streaming vs non-streaming, batches: 1/4. sample: 1k prompts from canary promptset + 200 long-arg synthetic prompts.
Javi: running schema-coverage-checker v0.3.1, collecting parse_failure_class, token-boundary fingerprints, and trailing-comma heuristics.
bench-bot: run 1806123456-A started on pool canary-g2
Mira: quick numbers from initial non-stream run: int8 non-stream parse_success 98.2%, int4 non-stream 88.7%. streaming makes it worse: int4 stream 79.6%.
Tess: that's a big delta for streaming. is it chunk-boundary splitting?
Mira: looks that way. examples show mid-string splits that leave unbalanced quotes in chunk middle. snippet:
```
{ "tool_call": { "name": "create_alert", "args": "{\"title\": \"Disk full on svc-7\", \"meta\": \"path: /var/logs/app.log\"}" } }
```
Arjun: streaming client can't reassemble because we don't encode message framing. we rely on the caller to buffer until final chunk; but if model delays closing-quote tokens, client sees an invalid JSON segment.
Javi: hypothesis: int4 changes token emission timing due to tokenization probability shifts; that creates more mid-word chunk boundaries. Also saw a class of malformed trailing commas from int4 non-stream (~0.35% of sample).
Mira: tried two mitigations server-side: 1) conservative-flush (do not flush a stream chunk if it leaves JSON unparseable within a lookahead of 64 bytes), 2) repair-suffix (on finalization, attempt small suffix edits to close quotes/arrays).
bench-bot: run 1806123456-B (conservative-flush) started
Mira: conservative-flush increased int4 stream parse_success -> 92.5% but p95 latency +180ms. repair-suffix bumped success slightly to 93.1% with +35ms at finalization but introduces small semantic risk. retry budget use dropped by ~40% vs baseline.
Tess: UX check: is ~93% acceptable for streaming? fallback rate to non-streaming?
Mira: fallback to non-stream used for 0.9% of requests in conservative-flush run; cost delta ~+4% due to extra tokens and occasional int8 fallback.
Lin: any observed API error spikes during these runs? I saw a tiny increase in 5xx during repair-suffix tests earlier.
Mira: yes, transient worker oom on one canary host while buffering for conservative-flush. we increased per-worker buffer limit and that stabilized.
Javi: additional patterns: long args (>150 chars) are 4x likelier to break in int4 stream vs int8 stream. also saw weird comma insertion in arrays from int4 non-stream in a small percentage; I've filed RW-7122 for model-output cleanup.
Mira: next steps: 1) checkpoint: enable conservative-flush behind an opt-in per-customer flag; 2) run int4 kernel-padding calibration to reduce token-probability jitter; 3) expand regression set with more long-arg and nested-json prompts; 4) schedule nightly sweep to measure p50/p95 latency + parse success across modes.
Arjun: infra: scheduled nightly canary sweep at 23:00 PT. bench-bot: job 1806123456-C queued for 23:00 PT.
bench-bot: job 1806123816 finished. artifacts at s3://redwood-canary/1806123456/ (schema-coverage-report + token-fingerprints).
Mira: final note: int4 non-stream residual class with trailing commas and occasional extra-escape sequences remains. research assigned RW-7122.
Tess: thanks, team. we'll review artifacts in tomorrow's triage. :eyes:
